zpnbc7: Original SpanishCue text. Read to understand the experience and the decision; then go back to the details.
b2n806: The bridge in the Molino neighborhood reopened yesterday after being closed for an afternoon. A neighbor had called the city council because one of the railings was moving. At first the news spread on social media that the bridge had collapsed. However, the photos that several users shared were of a repair from the previous year.
mqvgdw: When the technicians arrived, there were quite a lot of people on both sides of the river. Some neighbors needed to cross to get home; others had come over out of curiosity. The police closed off access while the team inspected the structure. A shopkeeper explained that she had heard a bang, but admitted she had not seen any collapse. The technicians found a loose piece in the railing and replaced it. There were no injuries and no damage to the central section.
1nae51p: A witness who works near the bridge asked not to appear in the photographs. The witness agreed to explain what she had seen, but carefully separated her account from other people's comments.
7wzv21: This week the neighborhood association has received several questions about the safety of the route. Its spokesperson recommends checking the city's notices before sharing alarming messages. It also proposes putting up a sign with the date of each inspection. The incident shows that information can seem urgent without being accurate. The important news is not only that the bridge reopened, but that a timely call allowed a small problem to be repaired before it became a bigger one.
